Hosmer-Lemeshow-type goodness-of-fit test for multinomial models

Source: R/tests_fit.R
hl_test.Rd

The test of Fagerland, Hosmer and Bofin (2008): cases are sorted by the fitted probability of the base alternative and split into groups groups of equal size; the weighted observed and expected counts of every alternative in every group give a Pearson statistic that is approximately chi-square on \((g - 2)(J - 1)\) degrees of freedom under a correct model. Small expected counts (below 5) are reported; the test is a calibration check, not a test of IIA.

Usage

hl_test(object, groups = 10L)

Arguments

object

A fitted choice model with independent single choices: not a remnl() or rologit() fit, and not a penalized fit (firth = TRUE or a prior). The cases are taken as independent; a fit's cluster does not enter the statistic.

groups

Number of groups (default 10).

Value

A list of class "hl_test" with statistic, df, p.value, observed and expected (group by alternative), and n_small (expected counts below 5).

References

Fagerland, M.W., Hosmer, D.W. and Bofin, A.M. (2008). Multinomial goodness-of-fit tests for logistic regression models. Statistics in Medicine, 27, 4238-4253. doi:10.1002/sim.3202

See also

Other specification tests: captivity_test(), combine_test(), rank_test(), term_test()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- rmnl(1500, beta = cbind(b = c(0.5, -1, 0.8), c = c(-0.3, 0.6, -0.5)))
hl_test(mnl(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d))
#> Fagerland-Hosmer-Bofin goodness-of-fit test (10 groups by the base alternative's fitted probability)
#>   statistic = 10.332 on 16 df, p = 0.849
#>   1 expected count(s) below 5.
